title: De Gaulle: I write your name
gist: A short culture notebook praising the second part of Antonin Baudry's de Gaulle biopic, with brief notes on Edwin Muir's First Poems and Bob Dylan's debut album. No market-relevant content.

insights.claim: Antonin Baudry's two-part de Gaulle biopic ends with De Gaulle: Liberté, judged even better than the first part, Résistance, and restores the heroism of French forces, with Niels Schneider as General Leclerc and Félix Kysyl as Jean Moulin.
insights.speaker: Alastair Benn
insights.so_what: Cultural signal of continued French interest in Gaullist national narrative.
insights.locator: The second instalment of Antonin Baudry's two-part biopic

insights.claim: The film's French subtitle 'J'écris ton nom' refers to Paul Éluard's 1942 poem 'Liberté', published under the German Occupation.
insights.speaker: Alastair Benn
insights.locator: The French subtitle is 'J'écris ton nom'

insights.claim: The author views Edwin Muir's First Poems, published when he was 37, as already mature and worldly, with a Homeric obsession running through his later work, and sees Bob Dylan's 1962 debut as flawed but promising, with a December London concert possibly a farewell.
insights.speaker: Alastair Benn
insights.so_what: Light cultural commentary; no investment relevance.
